t.E304.agn: In 2015 EFSA could not set an acceptable daily intake (ADI) because toxicological data were limited; however, it found no safety concern at the reported use levels.
t.E304.body: It is assumed to break down during digestion into ascorbic acid (vitamin C) and a fatty acid (palmitic or stearic acid).
t.E304.prod: Obtained by esterifying ascorbic acid with palmitic acid (chemically or enzymatically).
t.E304.regx.0: Re-evaluated; data insufficient to set an ADI, no safety concern at the reported uses.
t.E304.summary: The fat-soluble form of vitamin C (ascorbyl palmitate, etc.). It delays fats going rancid.
t.E304.what: It is a fat-soluble ester of vitamin C; it is an antioxidant that delays fats going rancid.
